title: Perfect derived tensor and surjective module inverse limits
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $D(A)$ be the unbounded derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $C\in D(A)$ be perfect, meaning represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Let $(N_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an inverse sequence of $A$-modules with surjective transitions and $N=\varprojlim_nN_n$. Derived tensor is computed by projective resolutions, and $R\varprojlim$ is computed by the homotopy fibre of $1-s$ on the product of the complexes, where $s$ is induced by the transition maps [def-weil-derived-limit]. The comparison induced by $N\to N_n$ is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$,
$$C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_n[0]).$$
Here the comparison uses the strict inverse sequence and its resolution-derived inverse limit, so it is compatible with the projections and with morphisms of strict inverse sequences.

source.place: Tag 0D2L, lemma-pseudo-coherent-tensor-limit, restricted to perfect complexes and surjective module towers; the surjectivity identifies the module derived limit with its ordinary inverse limit.

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite-projective representative $P^\bullet$ of $C$ using [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Each $P^i$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P$ K-flat. The quasi-isomorphism criterion in [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] shows that tensoring $P$ with a projective resolution of any module $M$ gives a quasi-isomorphism to $P\otimes_A M[0]$. Thus the latter complex, with degree-$i$ term $P^i\otimes_A M$ and differential $d_P\otimes1$, computes $C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0]$. Use this one representative simultaneously for $M=N$ and every $N_n$, so the transitions are exactly $1\otimes t_n$.

source.place: Tag 0CYB, lemma-pseudo-coherent-tensor, proof of (1) implies (2); Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism

proof.text: Put $B=\prod_nN_n$ and $v:B\to B$, $v(x)_n=x_n-t_nx_{n+1}$. By the definition of the ordinary inverse limit, $N=\ker v$. For every $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-finitely-presented] makes $P^i$ finitely presented, and [lem-trf-finite-presentation-tensor-products] identifies $P^i\otimes_A B$ with $\prod_n(P^i\otimes_A N_n)$ by the map $p\otimes(x_n)\mapsto(p\otimes x_n)_n$. Under this map $1\otimes v$ is $1-s$ for the tensor tower: their $n$th coordinates on a pure tensor are both $p\otimes x_n-p\otimes t_nx_{n+1}$. By flatness from step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring $0\to N\to B\xrightarrow v B$ identifies $P^i\otimes_A N$ with the kernel of this tensor-tower endomorphism, namely $\lim_n(P^i\otimes_A N_n)$. The resulting bijection $\alpha^i$ is the canonical projection map. Its coordinates commute with $d_P\otimes1$, so these bijections assemble to a chain isomorphism $\alpha:P\otimes_A N\xrightarrow{\sim}L:=\lim_n(P\otimes_A N_n)$.

Let $K_n=P\otimes_A N_n$. The maps $K_{n+1}^i\to K_n^i$ are surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $N_{n+1}\to N_n\to0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-module-complex-tower-limit] with the constant ring tower $A_n=A$ and the strict complex tower $K_n$. Its hypotheses hold degree by degree; no assertion about surjectivity on cohomology is needed. It gives a distinguished Roos triangle with first object $Q(L)$ and first map the product of the actual projections $L\to K_n$. Hence the termwise limit represents the derived limit with the required projections.

To specify the comparison in the strict model, put $V=\prod_nK_n$ termwise and $v=1-s$. Use the shifted cone coordinates $F^q=V^{q-1}\oplus V^q$, $d_F(y,x)=(-dy-vx,dx)$, from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $j:L=\ker v\to F$, $x\mapsto(0,x)$. This is the canonical map underlying step 3, and it is a quasi-isomorphism as the following coordinate verification also shows. Each $v:V^q\to V^q$ is surjective: given $(b_n)$ set $a_1=0$ and recursively choose $a_{n+1}$ with $t_na_{n+1}=a_n-b_n$. For a cycle $(y,x)$ in $F^q$, choose $z\in V^{q-1}$ with $vz=y$. Subtracting $d_F(0,-z)=(y,-dz)$ gives $(0,x+dz)$, where $v(x+dz)=0$. Thus every class comes from $L$. If $(0,x)=d_F(y,z)$, choose $w\in V^{q-2}$ with $vw=y$. Then $v(z+dw)=vz+dy=0$ and $d(z+dw)=x$, proving injectivity on cohomology. Consequently $Q(j\alpha)$ is the required isomorphism to the strict derived-limit model. Its projection to $K_n$ is precisely $1\otimes(N\to N_n)$, not merely some morphism between isomorphic cone objects.

For a strict tower morphism $u_n:N_n\to N'_n$, the map on limits sends $(x_n)$ to $(u_nx_n)$, $\alpha$ sends $p\otimes(x_n)$ to $(p\otimes x_n)$, and the Roos map applies $\prod_n(1\otimes u_n)$ to each cone coordinate. Therefore both composites send $p\otimes(x_n)$ to $(0,(p\otimes u_nx_n)_n)$; these formulas prove naturality and projection compatibility. They also commute with every chain map $P\to P'$. By [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], morphisms between these bounded projective representatives give all morphisms between their derived objects, modulo chain homotopy. For a homotopy $h$ between such maps the induced Roos homotopy is $(y,x)\mapsto(-hy,hx)$; it commutes with $j$ and the ordinary tensor homotopy. Thus the same naturality identity holds in $D(A)$, is independent of the representative, and is natural in the perfect object as well. These constructions apply to the strict, resolution-derived limit stipulated in the statement; they do not choose functorial cones on arbitrary towers in a bare triangulated category.

The item is the case of 0D2L with K perfect and surjective transitions; its statement is unchanged and not weakened. Step 1: the bounded finite-projective P is flat termwise, hence K-flat (lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat), and the qis clause of def-pc-module-kflat-complex gives P⊗M[0] = C⊗^L M. Step 2: P^i is finitely presented, so lem-trf-finite-presentation-tensor-products gives θ, which intertwines 1⊗v with 1−s; flat left exactness of 0→N→∏→∏ then gives the chain iso α onto lim. Step 3: right exactness makes the transitions of K_n surjective, and the strict tower lemma with constant ring A gives the Roos triangle with the actual projections. Step 4: the cone coordinates d_F(y,x)=(−dy−vx,dx) are C(v)[−1]; I re-derived the recursive surjectivity of v and the surjectivity and injectivity on cohomology of j, with all signs; the projection to K_n is 1⊗(N→N_n). Step 5: tower naturality holds on pure tensors; naturality in C follows from the bounded-projective homotopy representative lemma, and I checked that the Roos homotopy (−hy,hx) is valid. Edge cases checked: A=Z, N_n=Z/p^n, zero objects, non-flat N_n; surjectivity is used only degreewise and is needed. No new nodes.
